title: Cmd+Return shows the selected result in its enclosing folder, and the command becomes a real action with a menu entry
problem: 'Show in Enclosing Folder' exists only as a right-click item on a single search or Recents result, wired with `on_click` instead of an action (src/finder/menus.rs:198-209). It is not an action (none in src/actions.rs:9-98), so it has no shortcut and no key hint, and it is missing from the menu bar (File menu, actions.rs:334-362) and from the toolbar's Actions menu (src/finder/toolbar.rs:708-828, where 759-770 offers only Copy Path and the system-file-manager reveal). In the results, Return, Cmd+Down and Cmd+O all open the file (actions.rs:184-186); getting from a hit to its folder always needs the mouse. Go > Enclosing Folder / Cmd+Up (`go_up`, src/finder/mod.rs:975-988) ignores the selected result: while searching it ends the search and opens the parent of the folder the search started in, and in Recents or sent Results it returns early because `current_folder()` is None. Jumping from a hit to its folder is the most common thing to do after a search; Spotlight uses Cmd+Return, Everything uses Ctrl+Enter, Finder has it in the File menu. The manual lists it only under the item menu (docs/manual.md:800) and the shortcut tables have nothing for it (895-924). Also, Up on the first result just clamps (`Selection::move_by`, src/model.rs:291-305; `move_selection`, mod.rs:1788-1824), so going back to refine the query needs Cmd+F.
proposal: src/actions.rs: add `ShowInEnclosingFolder` to the `actions!` list and bind `secondary-enter` in the FILES context (unused today; Cmd+Return on macOS, Ctrl+Enter elsewhere). Add `MenuItem::action("Show in Enclosing Folder", ShowInEnclosingFolder)` to the File menu after Get Info. src/finder/mod.rs: add `fn show_in_enclosing_folder(&mut self, _: &ShowInEnclosingFolder, window, cx)`: when `is_searching() || current_folder().is_none()` (the same condition as menus.rs:138: search results, Recents, results sent from Nushell) take `primary_entry()` and call `reveal_in_place(&entry.path, window, cx)`; register it with the other window-level `.on_action` handlers (mod.rs:3053 onward) so menus reach it from any focus. src/finder/menus.rs:198-209: switch the context-menu item to `.action(Box::new(ShowInEnclosingFolder))` so the shortcut shows. src/finder/toolbar.rs `actions_menu`: add the item next to Copy Path, disabled unless one result is selected. tests/controls.rs: add the action to the list in `every_menu_bar_action_has_a_handler` (227-281). Smaller additions from the third reviewer: in `go_up`, when `shows_parent_column()` and exactly one item is selected, call `reveal_in_place` for it instead (keep today's behaviour otherwise); in `move_selection` (mod.rs:1815-1817 path), when searching, moving up without extending and the cursor is already on row 0 (or the icon grid's top line, where `icon_step` returns None), call `focus_search`. Update the shortcut and menu tables in docs/manual.md and add a CHANGELOG entry.
original_test_plan: Headless UI tests in tests/finder.rs: type `atlas` in the search field, `ui.select("Project Atlas.txt")`, `ui.press(&cmd("enter"))`; assert `ui.folder() == Some(fx.path("Projects/atlas"))`, `!is_searching()`, `ui.selected() == ["Project Atlas.txt"]` and `ui.files_focused()`. Same from Recents-style sent results (`show_results`). In a plain folder press cmd(enter) and assert nothing changes. Right-click a result, assert `ui.menu_labels()` contains Show in Enclosing Folder, click it, and assert the same outcome. For the additions: with one result selected `ui.press(&cmd("up"))` reveals it, with nothing selected Cmd+Up still goes to the fixture's parent; type `atlas`, press down (row 0 selected), press up and assert `window.has_focused_input(cx)` with the query unchanged. Add the action to the handler-availability list at tests/controls.rs:227-281.
original_risks: Cmd+Return is unbound in the file views today, so nothing is displaced. In a `--pick` window Return chooses; Cmd+Return revealing instead is consistent (the handler only navigates) but should be mentioned in the picker notes. With several items selected it acts on the primary one. Cmd+Up changes meaning while a single result is selected. Up-to-field must fire only while searching, never in a folder listing. One reviewer placed the menu item in Go rather than File (File chosen, as two reviewers and Finder do). The third reviewer also proposed Cmd+Return in the search FIELD opening the top hit (`PressEnter { secondary: true, .. }`, gpui-base src/input/base/state.rs:132-137, ignored at mod.rs:1308); left out of the core proposal because the same key would then open in the field and reveal in the list. Revealing still ends the search unless back-forward-restore-search is also done.

verifier.claim_check:
Every factual claim holds; the proposal has one real bug and two extras that should be cut.

**What the code does today**
- "Show in Enclosing Folder" exists only as a context-menu item built with `on_click` on a captured path (`src/finder/menus.rs:198-209`). It is shown when `searching && single`, where `searching = is_searching() || current_folder().is_none()` (menus.rs:138).
- There is no such action in `actions!` (`src/actions.rs:9-98`), no File menu entry (actions.rs:334-362), and no Actions-menu entry (`src/finder/toolbar.rs:759-770` has only Copy Path and the system reveal).
- Return, Cmd+Down and Cmd+O all map to `OpenSelected` (actions.rs:184-186). `secondary-enter` is unbound in the app; the kit binds cmd/ctrl-enter only inside its own `List`, `Input`, `Select` and `Combobox` contexts, which the file views do not use (`mod.rs:3282-3288`).
- `go_up` (`src/finder/mod.rs:975-988`) ignores the selection. While searching it ends the search and opens the parent of the base folder; in Recents and sent Results it returns early.
- Up on row 0 clamps (`src/model.rs:291-305`, mod.rs:1815-1818).
- The manual mentions the command only at `docs/manual.md:476` and `:800`; the shortcut tables (895-924) have nothing. CHANGELOG has nothing. No test references the command.

**Where the claim overstates**
- "Always needs the mouse" is slightly too strong. Cmd+Alt+C, then Cmd+Shift+G, paste, Return reveals a file (`dialogs.rs:726`), and clicking the path-bar crumb does too (`bars.rs:259`, manual:138). Neither is a practical keyboard route.

**Bug in the proposal**
- `current_folder()` is also `None` in the Trash (`model.rs:24-29`). `item_menu` only avoids this because it returns `trash_item_menu` first (menus.rs:134-136).
- The proposed handler condition, and the `go_up` tweak via `shows_parent_column()` (mod.rs:774-776), would fire in the Trash and open the trash bin's backing directory as an ordinary folder.
verifier.implementation_notes:
**Core change (keep)**

1. `src/actions.rs`
   - Add `ShowInEnclosingFolder` to `actions!`.
   - Add `key("secondary-enter", ShowInEnclosingFolder, &files, cx)` beside the other file-view keys (around line 186). The `FinderFiles` predicate also matches `FinderFiles OnePane` and not `FinderFilesRenaming`, so inline rename is unaffected. `ctrl_alias` covers the terminal build.
   - Add `MenuItem::action("Show in Enclosing Folder", ShowInEnclosingFolder)` to the File menu after Get Info (line 344).

2. `src/finder/mod.rs`
   - Add one predicate used by all three surfaces: `pub(super) fn enclosing_target(&self) -> Option<PathBuf>`.
   - It returns the single selected entry's path only when `self.shows_parent_column() && !self.in_trash()` and `selected_entries()` has exactly one item. `in_trash()` is at `trash.rs:47` and is already false while searching from the Trash.
   - Add `fn show_in_enclosing_folder(&mut self, _: &ShowInEnclosingFolder, window, cx)`: if `enclosing_target()` is `Some(path)`, call `self.reveal_in_place(&path, window, cx)` (mod.rs:1005), then `self.focus_files(window, cx)`. The focus call matters when the menu bar dispatches it from the search field, since `end_search` clears the field but leaves focus there.
   - Register it unconditionally with the root handlers (mod.rs:3053-3148), as `put_back` is, so `every_menu_bar_action_has_a_handler` passes with focus in the search field. It is a no-op in a plain folder.

3. `src/finder/menus.rs:198-209`
   - Replace the `on_click` with `.action(Box::new(ShowInEnclosingFolder))`. The key hint then renders through `previous_focus_handle`, like Open and Copy Path in the same menu.
   - Delete the now-unused `let enclosing = first.path.clone();` (line 147) to avoid an unused-variable warning.
   - Keep the `.when(searching && single, ..)` visibility.

4. `src/finder/toolbar.rs` `actions_menu`
   - After Copy Path (line 764), add the item inside `.when(finder.shows_parent_column() && !finder.in_trash(), ..)` with `.disabled(finder.enclosing_target().is_none())`.
   - Do not add a permanently present row that is disabled in every ordinary folder. This menu is the only menu-bar substitute on Linux and Windows (manual:847).

5. Docs
   - `docs/manual.md:476`: mention the key, the File and Actions menus, and that it applies to Recents and sent results too (the code already does; the text says only "search result").
   - Also update `:780` (File menu), `:800`, `:847` (Actions list), the file-views shortcut table (after line 905), and the search-field key notes near `:324`.
   - Add a CHANGELOG entry under `[Unreleased] > Added`.

**Extras (cut from this change)**

- **Up on row 0 moving to the search field: drop.**
  - `focus_search` (mod.rs:1485-1490) does `select_all`, so the next typed letter replaces the query instead of refining it.
  - A held or overshot Up followed by Return no longer opens the first hit; it re-runs the search and needs a second Return.
  - It needs separate handling for gallery, icon top line and group headers. Evaluate it as its own candidate.

- **`go_up` revealing the selected result: drop, or restrict.**
  - Return in the search field auto-selects row 0 (mod.rs:1308-1317), so while searching Cmd+Up and Alt+Up would almost always change meaning.
  - If wanted, restrict it to where `go_up` is dead today: in the `current_folder()` is `None` branch, fall back to `enclosing_target()`. That covers Recents and sent Results and is Trash-safe through the same predicate.
verifier.test_plan:
All of this runs headless on Linux with the existing harness in `tests/common/mod.rs` (`Fixture`, `Ui::open`, `ui.press`, `cmd`, `ui.type_text`, `ui.select`, `ui.select_also`, `ui.selected`, `ui.folder`, `ui.files_focused`, `ui.right_click`, `item_id`, `ui.menu_labels`, `ui.click_menu_item`, `ui.system_calls`, `ui.update`, `ui.read`).

**New test in `tests/finder.rs`** (next to `searches_by_name_and_returns_to_browsing` and `results_sent_from_nushell`)

1. Search result:
   - `ui.press(&cmd("f"))`, `ui.type_text("atlas")`, `ui.select("Project Atlas.txt")`.
   - Capture `let path = ui.read(|f| f.selected_entries()[0].path.clone())`, then `ui.press(&cmd("enter"))`.
   - Assert `ui.folder().as_deref() == path.parent()`, `ui.read(|f| f.query().is_empty())`, `ui.selected() == ["Project Atlas.txt"]`, `ui.files_focused()`, and that `ui.system_calls()` is empty (nothing was opened).
2. Sent results: `ui.update(|f, w, cx| f.show_results("Sent".into(), vec![fx.path("Roadmap.md"), fx.path("Projects/atlas/Project Atlas.txt")], w, cx))`, select the Atlas file, press `cmd("enter")`, assert `ui.folder() == Some(fx.path("Projects/atlas"))` and the selection.
3. Plain folder: `ui.select("Roadmap.md")`, press `cmd("enter")`; folder unchanged, `ui.system_calls()` empty.
4. Two results selected (`ui.select` then `ui.select_also`): the key does nothing.
5. Trash guard:
   - `ui.select("notes.txt")`, `ui.press(&cmd("backspace"))`, `ui.update(|f, w, cx| f.navigate(Location::Trash, w, cx))`, select the item, press `cmd("enter")`.
   - Assert `ui.read(|f| f.location().clone()) == Location::Trash`.
   - This would fail with the proposal as written.

**In `tests/controls.rs`**

- Add `ShowInEnclosingFolder.boxed_clone()` to the list in `every_menu_bar_action_has_a_handler` (227-281).
- Context menu:
   - Set a query with `ui.update(|f, _, cx| f.set_query("atlas".into(), true, cx))`, `ui.click("view-list")`, then `ui.right_click(item_id("row", &path))` using the hit's own path.
   - Assert `ui.menu_labels()` contains "Show in Enclosing Folder", `ui.click_menu_item(..)`, and assert the same folder and selection outcome.
   - In a plain folder, assert the label is absent from the item menu.
- Actions menu: while searching with one result selected, `ui.click("actions")`, `ui.click_menu_item("Show in Enclosing Folder")` reveals it. In a plain folder, `ui.click("actions")` shows no such label.

**Existing tests checked**

- `tests/finder.rs:37-53` (Cmd+Up in folders), `tests/controls.rs:304-326` (Down from the search field) and `tests/basics.rs:1029-1039` (Up in columns) keep passing because neither extra is implemented.
- No test asserts the full item-menu or Actions-menu label list, so the new rows break nothing.
verifier.risks:
- **Trash:** without the `!in_trash()` guard, the key and the File menu item would open the trash bin's storage directory as a normal folder. This is the one real bug in the proposal as written.
- **Ctrl+Enter convention on Windows and Linux:** Explorer and GNOME Files use it for "open the folder in a new window or tab", and fffinder already opens a folder in a new tab on Cmd+double-click (mod.rs:1659-1663). Using Cmd+Return for reveal is a mild inconsistency and takes the key a future "Open in New Tab" shortcut might want. It is acceptable because the key is a no-op outside results views, so the two could later coexist by context.
- **Menu bar on macOS:** the File item is always enabled and does nothing in an ordinary folder, because handlers are registered unconditionally by project convention. This is the same as Put Back outside the Trash.
- **Context-menu target:** the item now resolves its target at dispatch time from the selection instead of a captured path. This is safe because right-click selects the row first (mod.rs:1680-1688).
- **Terminal build:** many terminals cannot tell Ctrl+Enter from Enter, so the key may be unreachable there. The Actions and context menus still work.
- **Unchanged limitation:** revealing still ends the search, and Back does not restore it.
- **If the extras were kept:** the `go_up` tweak changes what Cmd+Up and Alt+Up do during nearly every keyboard search, and Up-to-field can silently replace the query and break "hold Up, then Return".
